decisions.executionNote: Begin left-arm elbow-up approach toward the left basket, lifting and gradually pitching the open gripper downward; right arm stays parked.
Advance above the nearer right egg in the left basket while completing the downward gripper pitch.
Lower the open left gripper around the nearer egg with a nearly vertical approach, refining position from the head and wrist views.
Close around the centered egg, then lift vertically to check that it remains between the fingers.
The egg appears retained. Lift clear of the basket and carry it toward the holder with the left gripper kept closed.
Carry the retained egg over the back-left cup, slowing near the holder and keeping the right arm clear.
Lower the egg vertically toward the back-left recess, making a small centering adjustment while retaining the grasp.
The egg is aligned over the back-left cup; open to let it settle, then withdraw upward and away from the lid. Tracking suggests contact, so avoid further descent.
One egg is visible in the holder. Return the open left gripper toward the basket at clearance height and restore a vertical approach.
Approach the rightmost remaining basket egg from above, lowering gradually with the left gripper open.
Descend toward the selected egg with small centering corrections; keep the fingers open until surrounding it.
Close around the centered second egg, pause for contact, then lift gently to check retention.
The second egg is visible between the fingers. Lift clear of the basket and carry toward the holder with the gripper closed.
Carry the second egg over the empty front-left cup, away from the upright lid and the first egg.
Lower the retained second egg toward the front-left recess with small centering corrections.
Release the second egg into the front-left cup, allow settling, then withdraw upward and left without further downward pressure.
Two eggs are visible seated in the left cups. Return above the basket for the nearer remaining egg with the gripper open.
Center over the nearer remaining basket egg and descend at a near-vertical orientation, leaving clearance before grasping.
Lower the open fingers around the third egg with millimeter-scale alignment corrections.
Recenter slightly on the shifted third egg, close the fingers, and lift to verify retention.
The third egg is retained. Lift above the basket rim and carry toward the holder with the fingers kept closed.
Carry the retained third egg toward the empty back-right recess, maintaining clearance over the two seated eggs and keeping the other arm parked.
Replan from the interrupted pose using smaller increments, easing down toward the empty right cup while preserving the grasp and configuration.
Contact near the upright lid may have released the egg. Open and back away in small increments to clear the lid and inspect its settled location.
Three eggs are now visible in the holder. Withdraw toward the basket above its rim and restore a vertical grasp orientation for the last egg.
Approach the final egg from above, moving left and back within the basket while lowering the open gripper.
Make a small leftward correction and lower around the last egg, keeping the fingers open until the egg is centered between them.
Close on the final egg without descending further, then lift vertically clear of the basket rim to verify the grasp.
The last egg appears displaced toward the far rim rather than securely retained. Reopen and recenter over its visible position for another careful grasp.
Align the fingers to the egg in the wrist image without further descent into the rim, then close and make a short test lift.
The final egg is now between the fingers. Lift clear of the rim and begin carrying toward the empty front-right cup, maintaining a closed grasp.
The egg slipped back into the basket. Reopen and return above its new position for a deeper, better-centered grasp.
Move left and slightly toward the far side to center the last egg, lowering the open gripper gradually for a deeper grasp.
The egg is centered between the fingers but the rim limits descent. Close at the observed pose and test a slow vertical lift before transporting.
The egg was not retained. Open and rotate the grasp direction above the basket so the fingers can straddle the egg without the left rim blocking descent.
Continue the overhead grasp-direction change with smaller rotation increments after the continuity rejection.
Complete the quarter-turn grasp alignment and descend above the egg's current position, avoiding the left-side basket rim.
Use the rotated wrist view to center the egg between the fingers, then descend slowly for a deeper grasp clear of the rim.
Narrow the open fingers to clear the rim, recenter on the shifted egg, then close and test a small lift without forcing further descent.
Lift straight up slowly while keeping the grasp closed, checking whether this deeper rotated grasp retains the last egg.
The egg has shifted out of the pinch. Reopen above the basket and let it settle before recentering rather than transport an uncertain grasp.
Approach the settled egg vertically with a narrower opening to clear the rim, aiming for a deeper equatorial grasp rather than pinching its underside.
Correct the egg's offset between the rotated fingers without pushing down into the basket, then close and perform a short retention test.
Keep the fingers closed and lift slowly, easing slightly inward from the basket wall to check whether the centered grasp retains the egg.
The egg remains between the fingers after the test lift. Carry it clear of the basket while slowly unwinding the wrist, keeping the grasp closed.
Carry the retained final egg toward the empty front-right cup, gradually angling the fingers inward so the wrist can stay left and clear of the lid.
Bring the final egg above the empty front-right recess while completing an angled approach that keeps the left wrist clear of the seated eggs.
Lower the retained final egg into the front-right recess with a small centering correction, keeping the angled wrist clear of the lid.
Release the final egg into the front-right cup without pressing farther down, then withdraw upward and left to inspect all four placements.
Withdraw fully from the holder and allow the released egg to settle; its position near the right cup still needs visual confirmation.
The fourth egg is perched on the right rim rather than seated. Clear the left arm and bring the right arm up in elbow-up configuration to reposition it.
Approach the perched egg from the right side at clearance height while pitching the open right gripper downward; left arm remains clear.
Center the right gripper above the perched egg and lower with a moderately open aperture, avoiding the neighboring seated eggs.
Refine the right-hand alignment around the perched egg, close at its sides, and make a short lift before reseating it.
Lift the egg slightly off the rim, shift it inward and toward the front-right cup center, then lower gently while retaining the grasp.
Release the recentered egg into the front-right cup, pause to let it settle, then lift the right hand clear for inspection.
All four eggs appear seated. Raise the closed right gripper clear of them and approach the far side of the upright lid from the right.
Position the closed right fingertips behind the upper edge of the lid, using a slow lateral approach above the eggs.
Push the lid forward and downward along its hinge arc with the closed right fingertips, keeping the left hand clear.
The lid appears fully closed. Withdraw both hands into their own workspaces and begin a gradual elbow-up return toward the starting poses.
Continue the controlled return in separate workspaces, gradually restoring the starting wrist orientations while keeping clear of the closed holder.
Lower both arms toward their starting heights while smoothly removing the remaining downward pitch, preserving configuration continuity.
